You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

    title='ARC task-e9fb55f9 verified L-frame nested diagonal rule',
    content='ARC task-e9fb55f9 VERIFIED RULE, solved first submission after 3 demos. Input is a solid rectangle of interior color A with a one-cell L-shaped frame of color B on two adjacent outer edges. Output is obtained geometrically according to the frame corner. For a top/left L (corner at r0c0): set outer top row and left col to A, except corner (0,0)=8. Draw a new B-colored L one row/col inward: row 1 from col 2 through last col, and col 1 from row 2 through last row. Fill the remaining submatrix rows/cols >=2 with 8, then put A on its main diagonal, i.e. every cell (r,c) with r=c and r,c>=2. All colors other than 8 are the original A/B; dimensions are unchanged. Generalize by reflection to other L orientations: preserve the original outer L cells as A except their corner becomes 8; shift the B-colored L inward one cell along both axes; fill the interior beyond it with 8; draw an A diagonal parallel to the original main diagonal, oriented by the corresponding reflection. For bottom/left frame as in the verified 8x8 test: B=9,A=5; output rows exactly [[5,9,8,8,8,8,8,5],[5,9,8,8,8,8,5,8],[5,9,8,8,8,5,8,8],[5,9,8,8,5,8,8,8],[5,9,8,5,8,8,8,8],[5,9,5,8,8,8,8,8],[5,8,9,9,9,9,9,9],[8,5,5,5,5,5,5,5]]. Equivalent method: reflect a non-top/left input to top/left orientation, apply the canonical rule, then undo that reflection.',
    path='arc/task-e9fb55f9', global_=True,

)
